subject: ClearHealth pilot — request for region pin + strict routing exception
messages:
From: Sarah L. <sarah@clearhealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot ask — regional-only inference + strict no-fallback for PHI workloads

Hi Vanessa / Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re greenlighting a small pilot (2k requests/day) to validate Redwood for PHI-handling inference. Before we start, legal and security require a couple of operational constraints:

- All inference for the pilot must be served from us-east-1 only (regional pin).
- No automatic fallback to other model variants or regions is allowed — if the primary model is unavailable, requests must fail rather than route to a different model (we cannot accept model mixes).
- The model variant must be the quantized, privacy-reviewed build (redwood-quant-hr-l24) — we need to lock model selection.

Attached is the security questionnaire excerpt that lists these controls (ClearHealth_Security_Req_2028.pdf). Can Redwood confirm whether these are feasible as an exception in the hosted flow, and what the expected impact on latency/cost will be?

We’d like a short mutual action plan this week if possible so procurement can sign the SOW.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah L.
Head of Product Security — ClearHealth
attachments: ClearHealth_Security_Req_2028.pdf

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Pilot ask — regional-only inference + strict no-fallback for PHI workloads

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clarity and the attached doc. Copying Lauren, Stephanie, and Karthik to scope the work and surface any blockers.

Quick notes / asks from our side:
- Confirming we can treat this as a routing exception for the pilot (requested: pin to us-east-1, enforce model id redwood-quant-hr-l24 and disable fallback).
- We need to size the expected delta (cost and latency) — Stephanie, can you provide a first-pass estimate and list of audit/evidence we’ll need?
- Karthik — can infra provision a dedicated route or strict policy that rejects rather than falls back? ETA for dev work?

Sarah — if you can share any hard SLA needs (p99 latency, acceptable error rates, retention window), that will help us recommend either hosted dedicated capacity or a private deployment for the pilot. For starters, we’ll assume p95 < 300ms and retention 30 days unless you tell us otherwise.

Proposed next steps by EOD Monday:
1) Redwood sends a short design note + cost delta.
2) ClearHealth confirms SLA/retention and signs the MA plan.
3) We schedule a short ops handoff call to walk the playbook.

Thanks — will follow up with the internal checklist in a second email.

—

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Jul 2028 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot ask — Pilot routing exception checklist & quick requirements

Vanessa / team — below is a concise checklist and our immediate ask items to evaluate the exception. I’ve attached a draft ops playbook (ops-playbook-route-exception.md) with template rollback steps.

Checklist (what we need to confirm to proceed):
1) Model bind: full model ID to pin = redwood-quant-hr-l24 (no alias fallback).
2) Region lock: route policy must only allow us-east-1. Requests matching account/tenant must be marked with routing tag CLR-8891.
3) Fallback behavior: set policy to REJECT on capacity miss (HTTP 503 with structured error) rather than route to alternate model.
4) Logging & audit: turn on token-level trace for pilot, export KV cache miss events, and retain logs for 90 days (configurable).
5) Security evidence: provide the PR-generated quant report and model provenance bundle for redwood-quant-hr-l24.
6) Cost/latency estimate: rough % delta vs default hosted variant + expected per-req cost with no batching.
7) Rollout plan: canary (5% traffic -> 25% -> 100%) + automatic abort on inference-error-rate > 1% or latency p95 > 1s.

Operational notes / risks:
- REJECTing requests on capacity constraints will translate to failed customer requests during incidents; ClearHealth must accept the availability trade-off (we should document an acceptable fallback manual process).
- If the model is pinned and hosted capacity is saturated, we can offer a short-term Dedicated pool (reserved capacity) for the pilot. That will increase unit costs ~x2–3 depending on commit.

Attachments: ops-playbook-route-exception.md (contains sample response codes, monitoring dashboards, and rollback playbook).

Please advise on two quick items before we draft a final MA plan:
A) Is ClearHealth willing to accept REJECT behavior (vs. queued retries)?
B) Confirm retention window (we proposed 90d for audit).

—
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Product Operations — Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah L. <sarah@clearhealth.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Jul 2028 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot ask — regional-only inference + strict no-fallback for PHI workloads

Sarah / team — quick infra response and plan:

- Feasibility: Yes, we can implement a region-pin + model-bind + REJECT-on-fallback policy for the pilot in the hosted environment as an exception. Implementation will be a routing-policy flag and a small control-plane change to enforce model_id and region before routing.

- ETA: we can produce a design PR and test harness by 2028-07-25 and target a staged rollout to your pilot by 2028-08-01, assuming we get signed MA and retention requirements this week.

- Capacity options: for 2k req/day we can operate on shared hosted capacity initially (with REJECT behavior). If ClearHealth prefers no failed requests under any circumstance, we recommend a Reserved Dedicated pool; I’ll include a cost delta in the design note.

Action items assigned:
- Karthik: design PR + test harness (task RWI-3029).
- Stephanie: cost/latency delta + evidence bundle (task RWI-3030).
- Vanessa: finalize MA plan + confirm SLA/retention with ClearHealth (task RWI-3028).

Sarah — we’ll send the design note and a one-page MA by EOD 2028-07-25. If you want to proceed faster we can schedule a 30-min design call tomorrow afternoon.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Platform Engineering — Redwood Inference
